Definition: properly, something carved out, i.e. ore; hence, gold (pure as originally mined)
KeyPassages: Job 28:16; Song of Solomon 5:11; Lamentations 4:1; Daniel 10:5
BiblicalUsage: Kethem means fine gold, ore carved out pure as it was mined: Job 28:16 says wisdom cannot be valued with the gold of Ophir, with the precious onyx, or the sapphire: Song of Solomon 5:11 says his head is as the most fine gold, his locks are bushy, and black as a raven. Lamentations 4:1 cries, how is the gold become dim! how is the most fine gold changed! Daniel 10:5 shows a man clothed in linen, whose loins were girded with fine gold of Uphaz.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe fine gold is the measure of everything: wisdom is worth more than it, love's bridegroom is crowned with it, and Jerusalem's gold went dim when she sinned. I hold that the gold that never dims is the man in linen, girded with the gold of Uphaz.
RelatedBooks: Job; Song of Solomon; Lamentations; Daniel
